name: Graft
text:
Decision: We should build a single, living "Memory Map" document that links every key idea, fact, or skill we want to recall—not as a list, but as a web of relationships. Each node is a short, plain-language summary, and every connection explains *why* two things belong together. This turns recall into a journey through meaning, not a hunt for keywords.

Trade-off: It takes time upfront to structure and link ideas, and we’ll resist updating it when new insights arrive. But the long-term gain—faster recall, deeper understanding, and fewer forgotten threads—outweighs the friction. The map becomes the artifact that proves the work was done.
